exposure: uterine scar status (scarred uterus vs. unscarred uterus)
type of uterine scar (cesarean section scar, uterine fibroid enucleation history)
outcome: adverse fetal/neonatal outcomes (severe asphyxia or fetal/neonatal death)
cohort: The study included all 61 cases of complete uterine rupture identified among 227,983 deliveries across 13 hospitals in Beijing and Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region between January 2012 and December 2016.
finding: Complete uterine rupture in non-scarred uteri was associated with higher rates of severe postpartum hemorrhage and perinatal mortality, and a trend towards increased adverse fetal/neonatal outcomes, compared to rupture in scarred uteri.
followup_time: at birth or in the immediate neonatal period
